//: EXAMPLE — the external-CLI registry read by sk-cli-executor / sk-cli-orchestrator.
//1: DO NOT hand-edit the live file. Manage it only with the CLI verbs (Rule 1 — .sidekicks/ is the
//2: CLI write surface): `sidekicks cli-executor register|list|remove`. This example documents the shape.
//3: Live file is scope-resolved: root -> .sidekicks/config/cli-executors.json ; project -> projects/<active>/config/cli-executors.json.
//4: A MISSING file is not an error — built-in adapters remain available and runtime selection stays provider-neutral.
//5: No routing.prefer chain is shipped. Auto-routing prefers the current host when eligible, then uses capability, containment, availability, and a stable neutral tie-break. Operators may configure a local chain explicitly.

claude.//: kind=builtin selects the native Claude adapter as one peer. It may be preferred when Claude Code hosts the current session, but is not a persisted project default.
claude.//models-top: `top` = the tier ABOVE high. Map it only where the CLI truly offers one — set with `register <name> --model-top <id>`; executors without one leave it unmapped.
claude.//model_specialties: OPTIONAL per-tier job pairing — for each configured model tier, the jobs THAT model is best at, so the orchestrator picks an item's model_tier by fit ('right job on the right model'), not just generic complexity. Set with `register <name> --model-specialties-high 'a,b' --model-specialties-mid '...' --model-specialties-low '...'` (empty value clears a tier). Advisory metadata — drives no flag.

codex.//: kind=builtin only toggles a native adapter (codex/gemini/antigravity). Omit to keep the default; set enabled:false to silence it.
codex.//models: OPTIONAL per-complexity model map, TIER KEYS ONLY — the map is rendered into a live registry, so a comment key inside it becomes a bogus tier. The orchestrator picks a tier by task difficulty; the executor resolves tier->id here and passes the CLI's model flag (codex -m, gemini -m, agy --model). Set with `register codex --model-high <id> --model-mid <id> --model-low <id>`.
codex.//models1: IDs are machine/account-specific. An absent map or unmapped tier means no flag -> the CLI's own default for sk-cli-executor; the GOAL engine instead fails closed, so an unmapped tier makes this family ineligible for that role.
codex.//specialties: OPTIONAL capability hints the orchestrator routes tasks against (via `list --json`) — short phrases, no closed vocabulary, drive no flag. Set with `register codex --specialties 'a,b,c'`.

my-cli.//: kind=generic is a NEW CLI driven entirely by this spec via adapter_generic.py — no bespoke adapter.
my-cli.//enabled: DISABLED on purpose: this entry documents the generic shape and its binary does not exist. This file is RENDERED into a forged core's live registry, so an enabled placeholder would arrive there as a real executor. Set enabled:true only on a spec you actually installed.
my-cli.//invoke: Arg template. Placeholders: {brief}=brief text, {brief_file}=path to brief on disk, {work_dir}=abs workspace, {model}=resolved model id. Must contain {brief} or {brief_file}, OR set brief_stdin:true.
my-cli.//model: Keep the model flag+value in ONE token (`--model={model}`): when no model resolves, the whole token is dropped, leaving no orphaned flag. A CLI with no model flag simply omits {model}.
my-cli.//probe: Optional side-effect-free reachability/auth check; exit 0 == available. Omit to treat 'binary on PATH' as available. Never runs a task turn.
my-cli.//sandbox: Informational containment label recorded on the result: kernel-sandbox | vm-isolation | cli-sandbox | constraint-block-only | unknown.
